companies.name: Krasny Defence Technologies Ltd
companies.note: Navi Mumbai Tier I MoD supplier: lifecycle support, refits and indigenous manufacturing for the Navy and Coast Guard; valuation at the round.

companies.name: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd
companies.note: Mumbai defence PSU building submarines, destroyers and frigates for the Navy; the largest listed naval yard and the same customer.

companies.name: Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd
companies.note: Kolkata Navratna defence PSU building warships and patrol vessels for the Navy and Coast Guard; same customer base.

companies.name: Cochin Shipyard Ltd
companies.note: Kochi PSU yard (built INS Vikrant) with a large ship-repair and refit business; the closest listed match to Krasny's refit work.

companies.name: Data Patterns (India) Ltd
companies.note: Chennai private defence electronics maker (radars, EW, avionics, naval systems); private-sector, high-margin defence supplier.

companies.name: Apollo Micro Systems Ltd
companies.note: Hyderabad private defence electronics and weapons-systems supplier (incl. naval programmes); the smallest listed peer by revenue.

dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: Krasny does refits, lifecycle support and indigenous manufacturing of sub-systems. Mazagon builds submarines and destroyers, Cochin built the INS Vikrant carrier, and Data Patterns designs its own radar and EW electronics.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: Krasny's revenue is almost entirely MoD, Navy and Coast Guard, at a much smaller revenue base. The shipyards also depend on the Navy, while Cochin adds commercial, export and repair customers and the electronics makers sell to DRDO, DPSUs and export buyers.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: Krasny's Tier I MoD status and Navy track record are real barriers for a services vendor. Yard capacity (docks and slipways) and decades of warship programmes protect the three PSU yards far more strongly.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: Krasny works from Navi Mumbai for domestic naval and Coast Guard units. The PSU yards have nomination-level access to MoD programmes, and Cochin and GRSE also take export and commercial orders.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: Krasny's FY26 revenue of ₹133 Cr is about 15% of Apollo's ₹904 Cr, the smallest peer, and about 1% of Mazagon's ₹13,008 Cr.

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: Krasny's FY26 accounts are unaudited, two sources differ by about 9% on revenue, and consolidated PAT is well above standalone. The listed peers publish audited results, PSU accounts also face C&AG review, and all carry listed-company disclosure.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: Krasny projects FY27E revenue of ₹352 Cr (+165%) against a ~₹2,250 Cr pipeline. Peers grew 4–61% in FY26, and Cochin's profit fell 13%. The projection is the company's own and unverified.

dims.name: Order book visibility
dims.why: Krasny's ~₹750 Cr firm orders cover 5.6x FY26 revenue, the highest cover in the set, against 1.4x at Mazagon and 4.4x at Cochin. The order book is as stated in the deal file, not independently verified.

dims.name: Profitability
dims.why: Krasny's 25.6% consolidated PAT margin is second only to Data Patterns (29.3%) and above Mazagon (19.8%), but standalone margin is 14.7%, closer to GRSE (10.7%) and Apollo (11.9%).

cells: Naval lifecycle support, refits and indigenous manufacturing
Frigates, corvettes, patrol vessels, survey ships
Carriers, naval and commercial ships, ship repair
matrix.why: Krasny is a services and sub-systems supplier, not a prime warship builder or electronics designer. Its work is closest to Cochin's repair arm.

cells: Unlisted; shares held by promoters and preferential allottees
matrix.why: Krasny has no listed-company disclosure. The PSU peers carry government ownership and oversight.

cells: Navy, commercial owners, exports, repair clients
matrix.why: Krasny has the narrowest customer base in the set.
Krasny is the smallest company in the set by an order of magnitude.
Krasny's 24% growth is mid-pack. The step-up to +165% is only a company projection for FY27E.
Relative to revenue, Krasny's 5.6x cover is the highest in the set; in absolute terms it is the smallest.

cells: FY26 unaudited; consolidated well above standalone
matrix.why: Investors are pricing Krasny on unaudited FY26 numbers, while every peer reports audited results.
Krasny's 35x FY26 P/E sits below the 42x peer median and above both PSU warship builders. It rises to 62x on standalone PAT.

cells: Secondary; exit via IPO targeted Sep 2028, then 6-month lock-in
matrix.why: Krasny buyers hold until listing and through the post-IPO lock-in. Peer shares can be sold any trading day.

cells: None to company; proceeds go to selling shareholders
matrix.why: The round does not fund Krasny's projected FY27 growth. That growth depends on operating cash and a planned debt raise.

barriers.name: MoD vendor status / Tier I supplier
barriers.note: Tier I standing with the Ministry of Defence lets Krasny bid for naval and Coast Guard work. Other qualified private firms and the PSU yards hold similar status.

barriers.name: Navy track record and references
barriers.note: A refit and lifecycle-support history with the Navy and Coast Guard counts in tenders. The deal file does not quantify how many platforms or contracts this covers.

barriers.name: Defence licensing and FDI limits
barriers.note: Defence is a licensed sector with FDI caps, which limits new and foreign entrants. The same limits apply to Krasny's own non-resident investors.

barriers.name: Infrastructure (docks, yards)
barriers.note: Krasny does not report dry-dock or yard capacity. Mazagon, GRSE and Cochin control most of the large naval docks, so Krasny competes on services rather than facilities.

barriers.name: Working capital and bank guarantees
barriers.note: Defence contracts need performance guarantees and long receivable cycles. A ₹133 Cr company has much less balance-sheet capacity than the listed peers, and the deal file mentions a planned debt raise.

ahead: Order book cover: ~₹750 Cr firm orders equal 5.6x FY26 revenue, against 1.4x–4.4x at the listed peers.
Consolidated PAT margin of 25.6% is above Mazagon (19.8%), Cochin (14.3%), Apollo (11.9%) and GRSE (10.7%); only Data Patterns (29.3%) is higher.
behind: Scale: FY26 revenue of ₹133 Cr is about 15% of Apollo's ₹904 Cr, the smallest peer, and about 1% of Mazagon's ₹13,008 Cr.
FY26 figures are unaudited. The memorandum (₹133 Cr) and the mandate holder's note (₹145 Cr) differ by about 9%; all peers report audited results.
Customer concentration: almost all revenue is MoD, Navy and Coast Guard, with no export or commercial business disclosed.
Liquidity: secondary shares with no exit until the targeted Sep 2028 IPO and a six-month post-listing lock-in.
watch: Signed FY26 audit confirming ₹133–145 Cr revenue and ₹34 Cr consolidated PAT, and the split between consolidated and standalone PAT.
Delivery against the FY27E projection of ₹352 Cr revenue and ₹66 Cr PAT (2.6x FY26 revenue), starting with H1 FY27 numbers.
Conversion of the ~₹2,250 Cr pipeline into firm orders, and closing of the planned debt raise to fund working capital.
DRHP filing on a timeline consistent with the Sep 2028 main-board IPO target.
valuation: Valuation per rupee of orders: 1.6x order book, close to GRSE (1.4x) and Cochin (1.4x) and below Mazagon (4.1x), Data Patterns (8.0x) and Apollo (7.9x).
P/E of 35x FY26 at the round sits below the 42x peer median, with peers ranging from 28x to 130x.
Standalone PAT of ₹19.5 Cr gives 62x P/E at the round, above every peer except Data Patterns (78x) and Apollo (130x).
